claims.source: Dave Beaty, Sean Munger and Craig Labadie, The Debrief, 9 May 2022
claims.text: Multiple USS Ronald Reagan watchstanders observed a round, orange, self-luminous object hovering above the flight deck and pacing the ship; witnesses include Karol Olesiak, Derek Smith and Patrick Gokey.

The Boatswain's Mate of the Watch says he was ordered by a senior officer to 'rip it out' of the logbook; another witness was instructed not to write the sighting down; Gokey says he saw an officer order subordinates to remove pages from the deck logbook.
Crew members estimated 50 to 300 additional personnel witnessed the event.

sources.name: The Debrief - Navy witnesses describe 2004 encounter aboard USS Ronald Reagan

desc: Between December 2003 and May 2004, while USS Ronald Reagan (CVN-76) operated in the Atlantic, multiple watchstanders observed a round, orange, self-luminous object hovering roughly 100 to 200 feet above the flight deck, pacing the ship at about 22 knots and performing half-circle manoeuvres before departing rapidly. Named witnesses include Quartermaster Karol Olesiak on the bridge navigation table, Seaman Derek Smith on the starboard forward catwalk, and Seaman Patrick Gokey, who observed it twice from different stations; two further witnesses remain anonymous. Crew estimated 50 to 300 people saw it. The reason this event belongs on the coverup strand rather than the sightings pile is what happened to the record: the Boatswain's Mate of the Watch says he was ordered by a senior officer to 'rip it out' of the logbook, another witness recalls being instructed not to write the sighting down, and Gokey says he watched an officer order subordinates to remove pages from the deck logbook. Deck logs are federal records. This is the aviator strand's clearest documented instance of the record being physically destroyed at the point of creation - the same behaviour the Princeton crew describe from the same year, in a different ocean, on a different ship.
